question: Can exposure-associated reproduction of Python function logic be detected when a code model does not reproduce the source nearly verbatim, and how does a checkpoint-level counterfactual signal change across structural, LLM-judged, and execution-based notions of equivalence?

key_findings.claim: The benchmark is an LLM-selected subset of publicly sourced CraneCode, not a representative random sample or a human-validated corpus of proprietary secrets.
key_findings.evidence: CraneCode is a filtered and rewritten Python subset of the-stack-v2-smol. From 100,000 sampled functions, the pipeline retains bodies of 10-50 lines and at least 500 characters, excludes __init__ methods, and asks LLaMA-3.1-7B-Instruct whether each contains meaningful proprietary functional logic and to assign severity 1-10; 7,422 pass. No human annotation, owner/confidentiality verification, inter-rater agreement, or false-positive audit validates inclusion or severity, so the experiment establishes logic reproduction more directly than proprietary harm.

anchors.section: A Filtering for meaningful functional logic

key_findings.claim: The exposed-versus-unexposed checkpoint comparison is materially stronger than inspecting one model, but it is not a per-function randomized counterfactual.
key_findings.evidence: The target is OLMo-3-32B stage2 ingredient1 step 23842, which has undergone CraneCode midtraining; the reference is stage1 step 656000, before CraneCode exposure. The target also differs through the rest of its intervening midtraining and broader code/domain adaptation. A larger target-reference similarity delta is evidence associated with the CraneCode-containing stage, but cannot by itself attribute every flagged function solely to that exact record.

key_findings.claim: Prompting supplies relatively little direct source context, but most examples still use the maximum allowed prefix and the function signature can itself be informative.
key_findings.evidence: Each greedy completion receives the target function signature without its docstring plus at most P=250 preceding tokens and generates up to 500 tokens. Appendix analysis reports that 91.6% of prompts hit the 250-token context cap. The model may therefore use file-local imports, class context, names, types, and signatures; this is a conditional-completion extraction test rather than context-free recovery.

key_findings.claim: Exposure shifts every reported mean similarity metric toward the training function, but average shifts are small and lack uncertainty for the paired target-reference difference.
key_findings.evidence: Across 7,422 functions, mean BLEU is 0.185 for the target versus 0.141 for the reference, the custom LLM judge is 0.209 versus 0.160, and HyClone similarity is 0.005 versus 0.002; CodeBLEU, TSED, edit, LCS, and other judges also move positively. Tables report cross-example standard deviations for some metrics, not confidence intervals, bootstrap intervals, repeated decoding, or significance tests for the paired mean delta.

key_findings.claim: Exact and near-verbatim counterfactual extraction exists but is rare under the stated greedy attack.
key_findings.evidence: The target emits 17 exact and 116 BLEU>=0.75 completions; the reference already emits 12 exact and 85 near-verbatim completions. Requiring the target to cross the threshold while the reference does not leaves 8 exact cases, 0.11%, and 43 near-verbatim cases, 0.58%. The raw target count alone would overstate exposure-specific extraction because some functions are predictable without CraneCode midtraining.

key_findings.claim: Functional-memorization prevalence depends by more than an order of magnitude on the chosen metric and prompt, so no single percentage is an interchangeable estimate of the latent phenomenon.
key_findings.evidence: Under target BLEU below 0.75 and functional score at least 0.75, CodeBLEU-DFG flags 130 functions, TSED 154, and the custom conservative LLM prompt 290 or 3.9%; the more permissive Nikiema prompt flags 1,040 or 14.0%. The union across all metrics is about 20%, while the union excluding Nikiema is 659 or 8.9%. These tests have different failure modes and calibration, and the union increases mechanically with the number and leniency of metrics.

anchors.section: 4 Results: structural and LLM functional metrics

key_findings.claim: Execution finds a small set of striking test-behavior matches, but neither low executability nor a 0.75 generated-test threshold establishes full functional identity or a calibrated prevalence.
key_findings.evidence: HyClone Stage 1 marks 276 target pairs and 166 reference pairs as likely clones. Only 42 target pairs yield any Stage-2 execution, of which 30 score at least 0.75; 21 target functions cross that threshold while the corresponding reference does not, 0.28% of all 7,422. Stage 2 generates ten inputs independently for each function and averages two cross-execution agreement fractions. Thus only about 15% of target Stage-1 candidates execute, failures mix non-equivalence with infrastructure failure, and passing means observed agreement on generated tests rather than equivalence over all inputs and side effects.

key_findings.claim: Text, structural, LLM, and execution metrics capture demonstrably different signals rather than progressively better measurements of one ground truth.
key_findings.evidence: Text metrics correlate at r>=0.70 and structural metrics at r>=0.75; LLM judges correlate moderately with one another at r=0.62-0.68, while HyClone similarity has correlations no larger than 0.17 with the others. Qualitative examples include exact constants and branch behavior with BLEU around 0.26 but high LLM and HyClone scores. Conversely, structural overlap can preserve calls while changing constants, and execution can miss untested edges.

key_findings.claim: Structural metrics lose coverage on malformed generations, can confuse scaffolding with semantics, and the paper reports internally inconsistent coverage numbers.
key_findings.evidence: The results text and Appendix E say AST parsing fails for 1,114 of 7,422 generated samples, which implies 6,308 successful parses or about 85.0% coverage; Appendix Table 3 instead labels structural coverage as approximately 92%. The appendix also reports 51 cases with TSED at least 0.7 but custom-judge score below 0.2 because shared call structure preserves syntax while strings or parameters change. Without a reconciled denominator, exact structural counts remain usable as reported but the summary coverage percentage is contradictory.

anchors.section: Table 3 and E Structural metric trade-offs

key_findings.claim: The LLM-based selection and judging pipeline is uncalibrated and shares model-family priors, creating correlated measurement risk.
key_findings.evidence: LLaMA-3.1-7B-Instruct selects meaningful/proprietary examples and assigns severity, while all three LLM similarity prompts use LLaMA-3.1-70B-Instruct. Prompt choice changes the counterfactual rate from 3.9% to 14.0%; Song and Nikiema scores differ by more than 0.3 on 28.4% of samples, and only 62 cases (0.84%) with BLEU below 0.75 pass all three judges at 0.75. No human equivalence labels, calibration curve, blinded code-owner review, or independent-model replication is supplied, so agreement among prompts is not independent ground truth.

key_findings.claim: The severity label does not predict a larger exposure-specific memorization signal in this benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: Across low, medium, and high severity buckets, target-reference deltas remain positive, but the correlation between severity and delta is below 0.06 in absolute value for all reported metrics. Because severity is itself a single LLM judgment and may covary with complexity or uniqueness, this is evidence of no relationship for that label, not evidence that actual harm severity is irrelevant.

key_findings.claim: Minimal preceding context strengthens the target-reference delta, while longer function bodies reduce textual recovery more than LLM-judged functional similarity.
key_findings.evidence: Context analysis reports the strongest BLEU delta, about +0.14, for minimal context and negative correlations between context length and delta. As body length grows, target BLEU falls from about 0.24 to 0.11 and its delta from +0.053 to +0.030, whereas the functional-judge gap is more stable. These post hoc strata are descriptive and can reflect selection and complexity, but support looking beyond verbatim metrics for long functions.

method.core_idea: Compare completions from a CraneCode-exposed OLMo-3-32B checkpoint with a pre-exposure checkpoint for the same selected functions, then require exposure-specific similarity under textual, structural, LLM-judged, or dynamic-execution criteria.
method.mechanism: An LLM filters CraneCode for functions it judges to contain meaningful or proprietary logic. Both checkpoints receive the same signature and bounded file prefix and greedily generate continuations. For each metric, a target is counterfactually flagged when the exposed checkpoint matches the training function above a functional threshold while remaining below the near-verbatim BLEU threshold and the reference checkpoint does not show the same match. HyClone adds an LLM screen followed by generated cross-execution tests.
assumptions: The stage1 checkpoint is a useful counterfactual for the stage2 checkpoint despite all intervening midtraining changes.
CraneCode inclusion metadata and the OLMo training recipe accurately establish exposure status.
The 7B judge reliably identifies meaningful proprietary logic and assigns meaningful severity without human labels.
A signature and up to 250 preceding tokens are a realistic and fair extraction prompt.
Greedy 500-token completion reveals relevant memorization without needing sampling or adaptive attacks.
BLEU below 0.75 adequately excludes near-verbatim reproduction when defining functional memorization.
A functional metric threshold of 0.75 has comparable meaning across structurally and semantically different metrics.
LLM judges can recognize behavioral equivalence and distinguish it from generic implementation similarity.
HyClone-generated tests exercise enough valid inputs to make matched outputs meaningful, while nonexecution can be treated as missing evidence.
A positive target-reference metric delta is more plausibly exposure-associated than a raw target match.

techniques.role: Subtracts predictability already present before CraneCode midtraining.
Selects code judged to contain meaningful or proprietary logic and assigns an unvalidated severity score.
Prompts both checkpoints with a signature and at most 250 preceding tokens.
Uses exact match and BLEU>=0.75 to measure direct textual extraction.
Applies CodeBLEU variants and normalized AST tree-edit similarity.
Scores functional equivalence under three published or custom prompts.
Screens likely clones and compares outputs on generated inputs.
Looks for low target BLEU, high functional score, and positive exposed-minus-reference difference.
Tests whether the measured signal varies with judged harm and prompt/function properties.

evaluations.setting: 7,422 LLM-selected CraneCode Python functions completed by exposed and pre-exposure OLMo-3-32B checkpoints.
evaluations.metric: Mean text, structure, LLM-judge, and execution similarity to the training continuation.
evaluations.result: All reported means favor the exposed checkpoint; BLEU is 0.185 versus 0.141, custom judge 0.209 versus 0.160, and HyClone similarity 0.005 versus 0.002.

evaluations.setting: Same paired completions under exact and BLEU>=0.75 criteria.
evaluations.result: Target counts are 17 exact and 116 near-verbatim versus 12 and 85 for reference; exposure-specific counts are 8 exact and 43 near-verbatim.
evaluations.baseline: Reference completion for the same function.

evaluations.setting: Target BLEU<0.75 with CodeBLEU, TSED, and three LLM functional judges.
evaluations.metric: Count crossing functional threshold 0.75 for target but not reference.
evaluations.result: Counts range from 28 for equal-weight CodeBLEU to 1,040 for the lenient Nikiema prompt; the custom judge flags 290, and the union excluding Nikiema is 659 or 8.9%.
evaluations.baseline: The same functional metric on the reference completion plus the target near-verbatim exclusion.

evaluations.setting: HyClone LLM screen and generated dynamic cross-execution on both checkpoints.
evaluations.metric: Stage-1 clone count, successful execution, and similarity>=0.75.
evaluations.result: 276 target pairs enter Stage 2, 42 yield any execution, 30 cross 0.75, and 21 are exposure-specific (0.28% of 7,422); reference counts are 166 screened, 21 executable, and 12 above threshold. Passing reflects generated-test output agreement, not proof over the input domain.
evaluations.baseline: Reference-checkpoint completion and HyClone Stage-1-only judgments.

evaluations.result: The stated 1,114 failures imply 6,308 successes, or about 85.0% coverage, contradicting the approximately 92% coverage printed in Appendix Table 3.
evaluations.baseline: Internal comparison of the results text and Appendix E against Table 3.

evaluations.setting: Cross-metric analysis over all function pairs.
evaluations.metric: Pearson correlation among text, structure, LLM, and execution metrics.
evaluations.result: Within-family metrics correlate strongly, LLM judges moderately, and HyClone no more than 0.17 with the rest, demonstrating materially distinct signals.
evaluations.baseline: BLEU as the conventional near-verbatim indicator.

evaluations.setting: Appendix case studies of network logic, geocoding, pricing, commissions, and classifiers.
evaluations.metric: Per-example target/reference text, structure, LLM, and HyClone scores plus code inspection.
evaluations.result: Several targets reproduce distinctive constants or branch behavior with low text overlap while references fail; the examples establish possibility, not frequency or representative harm.
evaluations.baseline: Ground-truth training function and pre-exposure completion.

evaluations.setting: Severity, prefix length, signature length, and function-body length strata.
evaluations.metric: Mean similarity and exposed-minus-reference delta by bucket.
evaluations.result: Severity has near-zero association with delta; minimal context strengthens the signal; longer bodies reduce BLEU and BLEU delta more than functional-judge delta.
evaluations.baseline: Other buckets within the same selected corpus.

limitations: Author-stated: dynamic execution covers only a small fraction of real-world functions because dependencies, state, complex inputs, and sandboxing fail.

Author-stated: structural metrics can produce false positives on shallow scaffolding, LLM judges are prompt-sensitive and nondeterministic, and execution has high false-negative risk from low coverage.

Reviewer-identified: CraneCode is publicly sourced and the selected subset is defined by one LLM judge; there is no human or code-owner validation of proprietary status, confidentiality, equivalence, or severity.
Reviewer-identified: exposed and reference checkpoints differ by an entire midtraining interval, not only controlled inclusion of each target function.
Reviewer-identified: no repeated decoding, prompt perturbation, checkpoint replication, bootstrap interval, or paired significance test quantifies uncertainty.
Reviewer-identified: 91.6% of prompts use the maximum prefix, and signatures can leak substantial semantic information.
Reviewer-identified: the 0.75 threshold is inherited or chosen but not calibrated to human functional-equivalence judgments for this corpus.
Reviewer-identified: HyClone agreement on generated tests cannot establish equivalence for all inputs, exceptions, state mutations, nondeterminism, or side effects.
Reviewer-identified: the stated 1,114 AST failures imply about 85% structural coverage, contradicting the approximately 92% shown in Appendix Table 3.
Reviewer-identified: three LLM metrics share LLaMA-3.1-70B and the selection judge shares the LLaMA-3.1 family, so their errors are not independent.
Reviewer-identified: unions across metrics do not estimate a well-defined prevalence because tests have unequal leniency, dependence, and missingness.
Reviewer-identified: qualitative examples are selected successes and cannot establish the distribution of harms.
Reviewer-identified: results concern one 32B model, one code corpus, one language, and greedy completion; scale and attack-strength trends are unknown.
failure_modes: Generic API conventions or obvious signatures can produce a functional match in both checkpoints without memorization.
Broad stage2 code adaptation can improve completion of a target even if that exact function had negligible training influence.
A structural metric can flag common scaffolding while missing a changed proprietary constant that reverses behavior.
An LLM judge can infer intended behavior from names and doc-like context and overrate a plausible but incorrect completion.
Generated tests can match on 20 attempted inputs while missing boundary cases, exceptions, state changes, nondeterminism, or side effects.
Dependency or sandbox failure can turn true functional clones into missing executions, making the observed dynamic count severely conservative.
The BLEU<0.75 gate can exclude semantically transformed clones with incidental text overlap or admit templated near-copies below the cutoff.
Taking a union over many metrics inflates counts as more permissive or correlated detectors are added.
Greedy decoding can miss memorized continuations available under sampling, beam search, suffix prompts, or adaptive prefix search.
Severity labels can reflect code complexity or model familiarity rather than actual commercial sensitivity.
reusable_insights: Use a pre-exposure checkpoint as a same-family baseline; raw target extraction counts otherwise mix memorization with ordinary predictability.
Report a vector of textual, structural, judged, and executed evidence instead of collapsing distinct notions of code similarity into one score.
Make the target-reference difference part of the flagging rule when exposure attribution matters.
Treat execution failures as missing evidence and separately report screening, executability, and behavioral-match denominators.
Include exact domain constants and boundary behavior in generated tests because scaffolding-level similarity is insufficient for proprietary logic.
Calibrate LLM-judge thresholds against blinded human equivalence labels and use model-family-diverse judges.
Prospectively stratify by prompt context and function length because text extraction sensitivity changes across those dimensions.
Separate possibility demonstrations from prevalence estimates and from harm/severity assessment.
open_questions: Would leave-one-function-out or canary-controlled midtraining reproduce the same functional deltas while isolating record-level causality?
How do human experts label proprietary status and functional equivalence for a blinded, representative subset, and how do metric precision/recall curves change?
What fraction of Stage-1 candidates execute under dependency reconstruction, stateful sandboxes, symbolic inputs, or developer-supplied tests?
Do adaptive extraction attacks and sampling reveal substantially more functional memorization than one greedy completion?
How does functional memorization scale with model size, duplicate count, training order, code complexity, and number of exposures?
Can influence functions, gradient attribution, or targeted unlearning distinguish exact-record influence from broad domain adaptation?
Which metric predicts real code-owner harm, license violation, or security risk rather than abstract similarity?
Can metamorphic and property-based testing catch equivalence or divergence that 20 generated cross-input attempts miss?
Does removing signatures or file context reduce exposure-specific signal, and what threat model best matches deployed code assistants?
Are the same behaviors present in Java, JavaScript, C++, infrastructure code, and stateful class methods?

competitive_landscape.title: Traces of Memorisation in Large Language Models for Code
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct predecessor measuring extractable training-code memorization and near-verbatim recovery across code models.
competitive_landscape.difference: Al-Kaswan et al. build code extraction benchmarks and report substantial verbatim recovery from vulnerable prefixes, including model-size trends. The present work narrows to one transparent exposed/reference checkpoint pair and broadens the target from text to behavior, but lacks the predecessor's multi-model scale comparison.

competitive_landscape.title: Unveiling Memorization in Code Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct multi-model empirical study of code-training memorization and extraction factors.
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. search large sets of generated outputs for verbatim training-code fragments and study model size, output length, prompt, and duplication effects. The present paper gains a same-architecture pre-exposure reference and semantic metrics, but evaluates only one 32B model and does not test those scaling or duplication factors.

competitive_landscape.title: Measuring memorization in RLHF for code completion
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest checkpoint-stage counterfactual study of code memorization across an additional training process.
competitive_landscape.difference: Pappu et al. track how textual code memorization surfaces and propagates through RLHF and direct preference learning. The present paper studies midtraining exposure and adds structural, LLM-functional, and execution evidence; it does not isolate alignment-stage mechanisms or use controlled preference examples.

competitive_landscape.title: How Much Do Code Language Models Remember? An Investigation on Data Extraction Attacks before and after Fine-tuning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct extraction-attack comparison before and after code-model fine-tuning.
competitive_landscape.difference: Salerno et al. benchmark pretraining and fine-tuning sample extractability under textual attack categories. The present exposed/reference design addresses a similar stage-change question but makes functional clone detection the central estimand; its functional rates are consequently not comparable to textual extraction prevalence without calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: Decoding Secret Memorization in Code LLMs Through Token-Level Characterization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct code-model extraction study targeting sensitive credentials rather than whole functions.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nie et al. distinguish real from hallucinated secrets with token-probability features and guide decoding to improve secret extraction across four code LLMs. The present work instead uses greedy signature completion and asks whether broader function behavior reappears; it does not implement an adaptive attack or verify that LLM-selected logic is actually confidential.

competitive_landscape.title: Memorize or Generalize? Evaluating LLM Code Generation with Code Rewriting
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct behavioral alternative to surface-similarity definitions of code memorization.
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. rewrite benchmark tasks semantically and define harmful memorization through high solution similarity plus failure on the rewritten task. The present paper instead knows a midtraining exposure boundary and compares generated functions directly with training code, but lacks the rewriting study's task-correctness/generalization control and multi-model comparisons.

competitive_landscape.title: Extracting alignment data in open models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest cross-domain extraction work using semantic rather than only string-space leakage signals.
competitive_landscape.difference: Barbero et al. use embedding-space distance to expose semantic leakage of alignment data beyond string overlap. The present work specializes that motivation to source code and adds AST and dynamic execution, while Barbero et al. study post-training alignment data and do not require executable equivalence.

competitive_landscape.title: HyClone: Bridging LLM Understanding and Dynamic Execution for Semantic Code Clone Detection
competitive_landscape.relationship: Primary source for the two-stage semantic-clone detector adapted as the strictest functional metric.
competitive_landscape.difference: Liang et al. evaluate LLM screening plus dynamic cross-execution as a general Python clone detector. The present paper reuses that machinery for exposure attribution between checkpoints; its severe real-world execution attrition shows why clone-detector benchmark performance does not automatically transfer to memorization prevalence measurement.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims clear evidence that a code language model can reproduce training-function logic without near-verbatim text, using an exposed/reference checkpoint pair and textual, structural, LLM-judged, and execution-based metrics.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Close code-memorization papers focus mainly on exact or approximate textual extraction across pretraining, fine-tuning, or RLHF. Combining transparent stage exposure, low-BLEU gating, structural and LLM judgments, and dynamic execution does expose compelling behavioral matches that text-only audits miss.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The checkpoint-counterfactual, low-text-overlap, multi-metric combination is the defensible novelty after comparison with behavioral code-rewriting and semantic alignment-data extraction predecessors. Prevalence and proprietary harm remain unresolved: selection is LLM-defined on public CraneCode, checkpoint differences are not record-level controlled, prompt-dependent rates span 3.9%-14%, metric unions are not a common estimand, and only 42 of 276 target HyClone candidates execute. The strongest conclusion is existence of exposure-associated logic reproduction, not a calibrated percentage of confidential logic memorized.

verification.passage_check: Independently reread the exact 32-page arXiv v1 PDF and extraction through references and Appendices A-G, including every selection/judge prompt, HyClone cross-execution denominator, seven qualitative examples, metric table, severity analysis, and prompt/continuation-length stratification. Recomputed all major percentages from N=7,422, narrowed execution claims to generated-test agreement, separated public CraneCode logic from verified proprietary status, and identified the unreconciled 1,114-failure/approximately-92%-coverage contradiction.
verification.competitor_check: Re-searched code extraction, checkpoint-stage memorization, sensitive-secret extraction, behavioral code rewriting, semantic leakage, and dynamic clone-detection query families. Verified eight primary arXiv records at their pinned current revisions: 2312.11658v2, 2308.09932v2, 2406.11715v2, 2501.17501v2, 2410.08858v2, 2503.02296v2, 2510.18554v2, and 2508.01357v1.
